subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `models status --probe --all` mode that performs live completion probes for every configured model candidate?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but adding this opt-in CLI mode defines a new live provider/model diagnostic contract with token cost, rate-limit, JSON, and overlap implications.

options.title: Approve narrow status probe mode
options.body: Add the opt-in `--probe --all` behavior in `models status`, preserving the default one-model-per-provider probe and requiring docs, typed output, and real CLI proof.

options.title: Fold into fallback diagnostics
options.body: Keep this issue open as design context and solve the verification need through a broader fallback-chain or model-migration diagnostic flow.

options.title: Decline core probing expansion
options.body: Avoid adding more live probing surface to core and steer users toward manual provider checks or future plugin/tooling instead.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow status probe mode
recommendation.body: Add the opt-in `--probe --all` behavior in `models status`, preserving the default one-model-per-provider probe and requiring docs, typed output, and real CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current `models status` auth probe behavior and has the strongest recent history across the affected CLI/status/provider surface.
